source.original_question:
A cake maker has rectangular boxes. She often receives orders for cakes in the shape of an ellipse, and wants to determine the largest possible cake that can be made to fit inside the rectangular box.

State the coordinates of the center of the cake in the form $(a, b)$.

adaptations.reason: Uniformly scaled original box40by20 and ellipse by1/5 to fit the fixed coordinate window, and updated centre from(20,10)to(4,2).

independent_solution.method: The largest axis-aligned ellipse touches all four sides of the box. Midpoint of xextents0,8 is4 and midpoint of yextents0,4 is2. Centre=(4,2).

audit.routing: Official Plane Geometry / Analytic source classification retained; coordinate diagram rendered under Analytics fixed-window protocol.
